public_rationale: The deadline is December 31, 2027. No evidence found by October 28, 2026 meets the early-resolution rule. Multiyear commitments and planned capacity are insufficient to establish that USD 200 billion will fall due specifically in 2027.
limitations: Contractual delivery conditions and amendments may change the amount payable.
Supplier backlog totals cannot substitute for the two customers' annual bills.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: At least $200 billion of OpenAI and Anthropic compute costs will come due in 2027.

statement.excerpt: Next year, at least $200 billion in compute costs are coming due.

our_interpretation: The surrounding passage identifies OpenAI and Anthropic, so the threshold applies to their combined obligations.
'Coming due' means contractual compute bills payable during 2027, whether or not ultimately paid.
The surrounding discussion presents estimates of private-company commitments, so the accounting basis is estimate.
criteria.support_condition: Reliable records establish at least USD 200 billion of combined OpenAI and Anthropic compute bills falling due during calendar 2027.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Complete records establish that their combined compute bills falling due during calendar 2027 total less than USD 200 billion.

evidence.excerpt: The agreement does not specify a fixed dollar commitment.
evidence.locator: Contractual Obligations, AMD Hardware Supply Agreement discussion, page 171
evidence.explanation: This qualification concerns Anthropic's AMD arrangement. It illustrates why announced capacity cannot automatically be converted into a fixed 2027 bill; it does not establish the combined total.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Complete 2027 payment schedules or subsequent records of bills due, covering both companies and reconciling delivery conditions and amendments.
